step0_classification.evidence: The rack software lives in weakly-connected worlds joined by one named bus: the OOB LAN is 'a separate physical Ethernet network ... usually air-gapped from the data plane' whose every BMC hangs off it, while DCGM's 'whole job' is in-band and 'the only relationship to OOB is negative' (source lines 271/277).
tie_breakers_considered: Density (E vs N): 11 historical relations over 13 concepts is neither a chain nor a fabric, so density alone does not decide.
A bus with disconnected worlds (tie-breaker 2) decides it: the OOB LAN is a source-named rail, the compute plane shares no edge with it, and the human in line 284 demands one bus that splits once.

Identifier density (tie-breaker 3) was rejected: the source carries no address, AS or port inventory that would outweigh the plane structure; the few identifiers (18 compute tray BMCs, :9400) are single facts, not a probe map.
step0_classification.secondary_recipe_applied: identity-probe-map coverage discipline (every identifier and qualifier gets a ledger row and a named view) plus service-mesh fan discipline for the controller's southbound API edges (stable port order, no merged bidirectional arrow). The dominant family stays placement-planes.
step0_classification.classification_history: No reclassification. placement-planes was named before the first spec and held through every attempt; the view split changed, the family did not.

views.title: In-band compute plane — exclusively in-band

Removing it would mean either giving up the one-split trunk the human demanded (line 284) or adding taps per branch (which the same human rejected).
